# DEGs

## T-Test Function

```{r}
# Function to calculate Fold Change and P-value for a specific virus at 24h vs Mock 24h
run_deg_analysis <- function(data_matrix, target_virus) {
  
  # Identify column indices for the target virus and the mock control at 24h
  idx_virus <- grep(paste0("^", target_virus, "_24h"), colnames(data_matrix))
  idx_mock <- grep("^mock_24h", colnames(data_matrix))
  
  # Apply t-test row by row (gene by gene)
  results <- t(apply(data_matrix, 1, function(gene_expr) {
    expr_virus <- gene_expr[idx_virus]
    expr_mock <- gene_expr[idx_mock]
    
    # Calculate log2 Fold Change (mean of virus minus mean of mock)
    # Since data is already log2 transformed: log2(A) - log2(B) = log2(A/B)
    logFC <- mean(expr_virus) - mean(expr_mock)
    
    # Run t-test (suppress errors if variance is 0)
    p_val <- tryCatch(
      t.test(expr_virus, expr_mock, var.equal = TRUE)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA
    )
    
    return(c(logFC = logFC, pvalue = p_val))
  }))
  
  # Convert to dataframe
  res_df <- as.data.frame(results)
  res_df$Gene <- rownames(res_df)
  
  # Apply Multiple Testing Correction (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)
  res_df$padj <- p.adjust(res_df$pvalue, method = "BH")
  
  return(res_df)
}
```

## Run T-Tests for each virus

```{r}
# Run the analysis for each virus vs Mock at 24h
deg_H7N9 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H7N9")
deg_H3N2 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H3N2")
deg_H7N7 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "H7N7")
deg_VN1203 <- run_deg_analysis(data_log, "VN1203")

# Check the top most significant genes for H7N9
head(deg_H7N9[order(deg_H7N9$padj), ])
```

## Significant dysregulated genes

```{r}
# Count how many DEGs each virus triggered at 24h, up or downregulated by more than double or half
sig_threshold <- function(df) {
  sum(df$padj < 0.05 & abs(df$logFC) > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
}

cat("Significant DEGs at 24h:\n",
    "H7N9: ", sig_threshold(deg_H7N9), "\n",
    "H3N2: ", sig_threshold(deg_H3N2), "\n",
    "H7N7: ", sig_threshold(deg_H7N7), "\n",
    "VN1203: ", sig_threshold(deg_VN1203), "\n")
```

## Venn Diagrams for DEGs

```{r}
# Extract significant upregulated and downregulated genes
get_up_genes <- function(df) df[which(df$padj < 0.05 & df$logFC > 1), "Gene"]
get_down_genes <- function(df) df[which(df$padj < 0.05 & df$logFC < -1), "Gene"]

list_UP <- list(
  H3N2   = get_up_genes(deg_H3N2),
  H7N7   = get_up_genes(deg_H7N7),
  H7N9   = get_up_genes(deg_H7N9),
  VN1203 = get_up_genes(deg_VN1203)
)

list_DOWN <- list(
  H3N2   = get_down_genes(deg_H3N2),
  H7N7   = get_down_genes(deg_H7N7),
  H7N9   = get_down_genes(deg_H7N9),
  VN1203 = get_down_genes(deg_VN1203)
)

# Plot Upregulated DEGs intersection
plot_UP <- ggVennDiagram(list_UP, label_alpha = 0, set_size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4FAFE", high = "#E41A1C") +
  labs(title = "Upregulated Genes at 24h", subtitle = "padj < 0.05, log2FC > 1") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot Downregulated DEGs intersection
plot_DOWN <- ggVennDiagram(list_DOWN, label_alpha = 0, set_size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4FAFE", high = "#377EB8") +
  labs(title = "Downregulated Genes at 24h", subtitle = "padj < 0.05, log2FC < -1") +

plot_UP
```

## Heatmap targeted on H7N9 dysregulated genes

```{r}
# 1. Combine the unique up and down genes into one list
h7n9_exclusive_genes <- c(unique_up_H7N9, unique_down_H7N9)

# 2. Subset the main log2 normalized matrix to keep only these genes
# We isolate only the 24h samples to keep the visual clean and focused
idx_24h <- grep("_24h", colnames(data_log))
matrix_24h <- data_log[h7n9_exclusive_genes, idx_24h]

# 3. Scale the data by row (gene) to highlight relative differences across viruses
# This centers each gene around 0, making patterns instantly visible
matrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(matrix_24h)))

# 4. Create annotation dataframe for the top of the heatmap
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  Virus = sapply(strsplit(colnames(matrix_24h), "_"), `[`, 1)
)
rownames(annotation_col) <- colnames(matrix_24h)

# Define matching colors for the annotation
ann_colors <- list(
  Virus = c(H3N2 = "#377EB8", H7N7 = "#FF7F00", 
            H7N9 = "#984EA3", mock = "#E41A1C", VN1203 = "#4DAF4A")
)

# 5. Generate the heatmap
pheatmap(matrix_scaled, 
         cluster_cols = TRUE,    # Cluster samples based on expression similarity
         cluster_rows = FALSE,    # Cluster genes with similar patterns
         show_rownames = FALSE,  # Hide 2,000+ gene names to keep it readable
         annotation_col = annotation_col,
         annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(50),
         main = "Expression Profile of H7N9-Exclusive DEGs at 24h",
         fontsize_col = 8)
```

## Volcano plots - 24h

```{r}
# Function to generate a standardized Volcano Plot
plot_volcano <- function(deg_df, virus_name) {
  
  # 1. Categorize genes based on our exact thresholds
  deg_df$Regulation <- "Not Significant"
  deg_df$Regulation[deg_df$logFC > 1 & deg_df$padj < 0.05] <- "Upregulated"
  deg_df$Regulation[deg_df$logFC < -1 & deg_df$padj < 0.05] <- "Downregulated"
  
  # Enforce factor levels for consistent coloring
  deg_df$Regulation <- factor(deg_df$Regulation, 
                              levels = c("Downregulated", "Not Significant", "Upregulated"))
  
  # 2. Extract the top 15 most significant genes for labeling
  top_genes <- head(deg_df[order(deg_df$padj), ], 15)
  
  # 3. Build the plot mapping magnitude (logFC) against significance (-log10 padj)
  ggplot(deg_df, aes(x = logFC, y = -log10(padj), color = Regulation)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Downregulated" = "#377EB8", 
                                  "Not Significant" = "grey80", 
                                  "Upregulated" = "#E41A1C")) +
    # Add threshold lines
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
    # Add non-overlapping labels for top genes
    geom_text_repel(data = top_genes, aes(label = Gene), 
                    size = 3, color = "black", max.overlaps = 20) +
    labs(title = paste(virus_name, "Transcriptomic Response"),
         subtitle = "24h post-infection vs Mock control",
         x = "Magnitude of Change (Log2 Fold Change)",
         y = "Statistical Significance (-Log10 Adjusted P-value)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

# Generate and display the Volcano plot for H7N9
volcano_H7N9 <- plot_volcano(deg_H7N9, "H7N9")
volcano_H7N9

# Volcano plots for other viruses
plot_volcano(deg_H3N2, "H3N2")
plot_volcano(deg_H7N7, "H7N7")
plot_volcano(deg_VN1203, "VN1203")
```

```{r}
# Inspect genes for a specific pathway as a clean vector
get_pathway_genes <- function(df, pattern) {
  hits <- df[grepl(pattern, df$Description, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
  setNames(strsplit(hits$geneID, "/"), hits$Description)
}

get_pathway_genes(res_down, "Neutrophil|glycosylation|carbohydrates|MHC class II")

```

Neutrophil degranulation : impossible because in-vitro cellular culture of epithelial cells

So what does it really represent ?

Neutrophil degranulation :

-   58 genes, almost all unexclusive to neutrophils

-   Endolysosomal machinery : Core lysosomal membrane proteins (`LAMP1`, `LAMP2`), V-ATPase acidification (`ATP6AP2`), lipid/glycan degradation (`NPC2`, `PSAP`, `ARSA`, `GLB1`, `GALNS`, `HGSNAT`, `MAN2B1`, `FUCA2`), and lysosomal proteases (`CTSC`, `CTSZ`, `DPP7`, `PRCP`).

-   Secreted airway epithelial defenses & antiproteases : `SLPI` (secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor), `SERPINA1` (alpha_1-antitrypsin), `SERPINA3`, `SERPINB6`, `CST3`, `TIMP2`, and `LCN2` (lipocalin-2), alongside the epithelial surface marker `CEACAM6` and complement inhibitor `CD59`.

    --\> So H7N9 may be **shutting down** lysosomal degradation and the secreted antiprotease/antimicrobial shield protecting the airway epithelium

### EnrichR (GO, KEGG)

```{r}
# 1. Define the reference databases to capture a multi-dimensional biological profile:
# - GO Biological Process (BP): Identifies the overarching systemic responses (e.g., immune evasion, cell death).
# - GO Molecular Function (MF): Highlights the specific biochemical activities of the dysregulated proteins.
# - GO Cellular Component (CC): Maps subcellular localization to show where the virus hijacks host machinery.
# - KEGG: Maps the gene lists to well-established signaling and metabolic pathways.
dbs <- c("GO_Biological_Process_2023", 
         "GO_Molecular_Function_2023", 
         "GO_Cellular_Component_2023", 
         "KEGG_2021_Human")

bg_symbols <- rownames(data_log)

# 2. Query the EnrichR API using the isolated H7N9-exclusive gene symbols.
# This statistically evaluates which biological concepts are significantly 
# over-represented in our specific viral signature compared to random chance.
enrich_up <- enrichr(unique_up_H7N9, dbs, background = bg_symbols, include_overlap = TRUE)
enrich_down <- enrichr(unique_down_H7N9, dbs, background = bg_symbols, include_overlap = TRUE)

# 3. GO Biological Process (BP): Systemic Functional Shifts
# Upregulated BP highlights active host stress responses or viral-driven cellular reprogramming.
# Downregulated BP pinpoints which host defenses or maintenance functions are actively suppressed.
plotEnrich(enrich_up[["GO_Biological_Process_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO BP: Upregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Biological_Process_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO BP: Downregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))


# 4. GO Molecular Function (MF): Biochemical Capabilities
# Upregulated MF uncovers specific enzymatic or binding activities recruited during infection.
# Downregulated MF reveals which functional molecular tools the host cell loses.
plotEnrich(enrich_up[["GO_Molecular_Function_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO MF: Upregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Molecular_Function_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO MF: Downregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))


# 5. GO Cellular Component (CC): Spatial and Structural Reorganization
# Upregulated CC maps organelles actively hijacked for viral replication (e.g., ER, Golgi).
# Downregulated CC indicates structural degradation or dismantled antigen-presenting locations.
plotEnrich(enrich_up[["GO_Cellular_Component_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO CC: Upregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

plotEnrich(enrich_down[["GO_Cellular_Component_2023"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("GO CC: Downregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))


# 6. KEGG Pathways: Established Macro-Signaling Networks
# Contextualizes the GO terms into known, documented biological network cascades 
# to definitively link the signature to established virological or metabolic models.
plotEnrich(enrich_up[["KEGG_2021_Human"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("KEGG: Upregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

plotEnrich(enrich_down[["KEGG_2021_Human"]], 
           showTerms = 10, numChar = 50, y = "Count", orderBy = "P.value") +
  ggtitle("KEGG: Downregulated in H7N9 (Exclusive)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
```

```{r}
# 1. Define reference databases covering biological processes, molecular functions,
#    subcellular localization, and canonical signaling/metabolic pathways
dbs <- c(
  "GO BP" = "GO_Biological_Process_2023",
  "GO MF" = "GO_Molecular_Function_2023",
  "GO CC" = "GO_Cellular_Component_2023",
  "KEGG"  = "KEGG_2021_Human"
)

# Restrict statistical background to genes actually measured on the array
bg_symbols <- rownames(data_log)

# 2. Query EnrichR for H7N9-exclusive upregulated and downregulated signatures
enrich_up   <- enrichr(unique_up_H7N9, unname(dbs), background = bg_symbols, include_overlap = TRUE)
enrich_down <- enrichr(unique_down_H7N9, unname(dbs), background = bg_symbols, include_overlap = TRUE)

# 3. Plot top FDR-significant terms with adjusted p-value color scaling
plot_enrichr_fdr <- function(enrich_list, db_key, db_label, direction,
                             fdr_cutoff = 0.05, top_n = 10) {
  df <- enrich_list[[db_key]]
  df <- df[df$Adjusted.P.value < fdr_cutoff, ]
  
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    message(sprintf("No significant terms (FDR < %.2f) for %s (%s)", fdr_cutoff, db_label, direction))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  df <- df[order(df$Adjusted.P.value, df$P.value), ]
  df <- head(df, top_n)
  df$Count <- as.numeric(sub("/.*", "", df$Overlap))
  df$Term_label <- str_wrap(df$Term, width = 45)
  df$Term_label <- factor(df$Term_label, levels = rev(df$Term_label))
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Count, y = Term_label, fill = Adjusted.P.value)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#e06663", high = "#327eba", name = "p.adjust") +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("%s: %s in H7N9 (Exclusive)", db_label, direction),
      x = "Gene count",
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, lineheight = 0.85),
      plot.title  = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
    )
}

# 4. Generate filtered plots across all four databases for UP and DOWN signatures
for (label in names(dbs)) {
  p_up   <- plot_enrichr_fdr(enrich_up, dbs[[label]], label, "Upregulated")
  p_down <- plot_enrichr_fdr(enrich_down, dbs[[label]], label, "Downregulated")
  if (!is.null(p_up))   print(p_up)
  if (!is.null(p_down)) print(p_down)
}
```

### Down-Regulation (H7N9-Exclusive Signature at 24h)

#### 1. Core Lysosomal Breakdown

-   **Primary anchor:** *Lysosome* ranks #1 in KEGG (\~23 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} < 0.0003$) and #2 in GO CC (\~59 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} < 3 \times 10^{-7}$, immediately following the parent term *Intracellular Organelle Lumen* at \~81 genes).

-   **Membrane and lumenal loss:** GO CC confirms strong suppression of both structural components (*Lysosomal Membrane*, \~44 genes) and the acidic interior (*Vacuolar Lumen*, \~26 genes; all top 10 GO CC terms at $p_{\text{adj}} \le 1 \times 10^{-6}$).

-   **Enzymatic collapse:** GO MF directly reflects loss of lysosomal proteolysis via *Exopeptidase Activity* (\~10 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} \le 0.004$), while Reactome captures core lysosomal hydrolases and membrane proteins (`LAMP1`, `LAMP2`, `ATP6AP2`, cathepsins, glycosidases) within *Neutrophil degranulation* ($\text{GeneRatio} \approx 0.100$) and *Metabolism of carbohydrates* ($\text{GeneRatio} \approx 0.057$).

#### 2. Upstream ER–Golgi Biogenesis & Secretory Bottleneck

-   **Organelle supply chain:** GO CC maps the entire biosynthetic pipeline upstream of the lysosome, encompassing *Endoplasmic Reticulum Membrane* (\~69 genes), *Endoplasmic Reticulum Lumen* (\~34 genes), *Bounding Membrane Of Organelle* (\~72 genes), *COPII-coated ER To Golgi Transport Vesicle* (\~18 genes), and *Secretory Granule Lumen* (\~37 genes).

-   **Post-translational sorting:** Reactome identifies *Asparagine N-linked glycosylation* ($\text{GeneRatio} \approx 0.060$), which is essential both for sorting soluble hydrolases from the Golgi to the lysosome and for shielding lysosomal membranes from self-digestion, alongside ER-folding and secretory spillover (*Regulation of IGF transport and uptake by IGFBPs*, *Maturation of spike protein*, and *Late SARS-CoV-2 Infection Events*).

-   **Loss of mucosal antiproteases and secreted barrier cargo:** GO BP (*Negative Regulation Of Endopeptidase Activity*, \~10 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} \le 0.0125$) and GO MF (*Endopeptidase Inhibitor Activity*, \~20 genes; *Serine-Type Endopeptidase Inhibitor Activity*, \~13 genes; *Peptidase Inhibitor Activity*, \~8 genes) confirm downregulation of secreted airway antiproteases (`SLPI`, `SERPINA1`, `SERPINA3`, `CST3`) routed through this secretory pathway. This is accompanied by ER/vesicle cofactors (*Calcium Ion Binding*, \~36 genes; *Metal Ion Binding*, \~51 genes), organelle transporters (*Secondary Active Transmembrane Transporter Activity*, \~10 genes), and suppression of secreted extracellular matrix/adhesion glycoproteins captured by MSigDB Hallmark (*Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition*, 25 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} = 0.017$).

#### 3. Downstream Immune Consequence: Endolysosomal MHC-II Silencing

-   Because MHC class II peptide loading relies directly on endolysosomal acidification and cathepsin-mediated cleavage, lysosomal suppression links directly to adaptive immune evasion.

-   This axis is independently confirmed across Reactome (*MHC class II antigen presentation*, $\text{GeneRatio} \approx 0.031$), five exogenous-antigen and MHC-II assembly terms in GO BP (7–10 genes each, $p_{\text{adj}} \le 0.0125$), and GO MF (*MHC Class II Protein Complex Binding*, \~8 genes; *MHC Class II Receptor Activity*, \~5 genes), driven by locus-wide transcriptional repression of `HLA-DR/DQ/DP` and `CD74`.

#### 4. Artifact Filtering & Secondary Non-Lysosomal Axes

-   **Epithelial context filtering:** In an *in vitro* airway epithelial monoculture, *Neutrophil degranulation* (Reactome) and *Azurophil Granule* (GO CC, \~29 genes) reflect shared endolysosomal and secretory machinery rather than neutrophil biology. Similarly, seven autoimmune and allograft pathways in KEGG (*Asthma*, *Intestinal immune network for IgA production*, *Type I diabetes mellitus*, *Allograft rejection*, *Autoimmune thyroid disease*, *Systemic lupus erythematosus*, and *Graft-versus-host disease*; all $p_{\text{adj}} \le 0.001$), four T-cell signaling hits in Reactome (*ZAP-70*, *CD3/TCR zeta chains*, *PD-1 signaling*, *Generation of second messenger molecules*), and two immunoglobulin terms in GO BP represent annotation echoes triggered by the same downregulated epithelial `HLA-D*` gene block.

-   **Distinct metabolic side axes:** Outside the endomembrane/lysosomal system, two secondary metabolic signatures remain consistently suppressed across databases:

    -   **Lipid and sterol biosynthesis:** Captured by KEGG (*Biosynthesis of unsaturated fatty acids*, \~8 genes), GO BP (*fatty-acyl-CoA Biosynthetic Process*, \~9 genes; *Long-Chain fatty-acyl-CoA Metabolic Process*, \~7 genes), MSigDB Hallmark (*Fatty Acid Metabolism*, 23 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} = 0.017$), and WikiPathways (*Cholesterol metabolism with Bloch and Kandutsch Russell pathways*, 11 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} = 0.030$), which directly interfaces with ER membrane synthesis and lysosomal cholesterol handling (`NPC2`).

    -   **Mitochondrial, amino-acid, and redox homeostasis:** Captured by Reactome (*Mitochondrial protein degradation*, *Phase II - Conjugation of compounds*, and *Glutathione conjugation*), GO MF (*Oxidoreductase Activity, Acting On The CH-OH Group Of Donors*, \~16 genes), KEGG (*Thiamine metabolism*, \~6 genes), and WikiPathways (two redundant *Urea cycle* entries of 7 genes at $p_{\text{adj}} = 0.030$, reflecting shared mitochondrial/cytosolic amino-acid handling rather than hepatic urea synthesis).

Taken together, the FDR-filtered multi-database enrichment profiles demonstrate that H7N9 uniquely destabilizes the host endomembrane system at 24h: by simultaneously suppressing ER–Golgi N-glycosylation, vesicular trafficking, and core lysosomal machinery, the virus impairs intracellular degradation, weakens the secreted epithelial antiprotease barrier, and silences epithelial MHC class II presentation.

### Up-Regulation (H7N9-Exclusive Signature at 24h)

#### 1. Massive Nuclear Transcriptional Reprogramming (and the KEGG HSV-1 Artifact)

-   **Overwhelming transcription factor (TF) signal:** Seven of the top ten FDR-significant GO BP terms ($p_{\text{adj}} \le 0.0035$) capture transcriptional control, led by *Regulation Of DNA-templated Transcription* (\~185 genes) and *Regulation Of Transcription By RNA Polymerase II* (\~185 genes), spanning both *Negative Regulation* (\~88–105 genes) and *Positive Regulation* (\~92 genes).

-   **DNA-binding confirmation:** All ten top GO MF terms ($p_{\text{adj}} < 3 \times 10^{-5}$) directly corroborate this nuclear regulatory shift, highlighting *RNA Polymerase II Transcription Regulatory Region Sequence-Specific DNA Binding* (\~136 genes), *Cis-Regulatory Region Sequence-Specific DNA Binding* (\~122 genes), *DNA Binding* (\~68 genes), and both *DNA-binding Transcription Activator* (\~39 genes) and *Repressor Activity* (\~31 genes).

-   **Strict nuclear localization:** Under FDR filtering ($p_{\text{adj}} < 0.05$), GO CC collapses to just two highly significant broad compartments—*Nucleus* (\~296 genes) and *Intracellular Membrane-Bounded Organelle* (\~316 genes, both $p_{\text{adj}} < 1 \times 10^{-9}$)—confirming that the upregulated signature is overwhelmingly nuclear rather than localized to specific cytoplasmic organelles.

-   **Artifact check (*Herpes simplex virus 1 infection*):** In KEGG, *Herpes simplex virus 1 infection* is the sole pathway surviving multiple-testing correction (\~64 genes, $p_{\text{adj}} = 3.74 \times 10^{-11}$). Rather than indicating herpesvirus biology, this is a well-known KEGG annotation artifact (`hsa05168`): KEGG bundles hundreds of KRAB-domain zinc finger (`ZNF`) transcriptional repressors into the HSV-1 map. Because the H7N9-exclusive upregulated signature is heavily enriched in nuclear DNA-binding repressors, these `ZNF` genes trigger `hsa05168` specifically while sparse TF annotation in KEGG and Reactome leaves all other pathways below statistical significance.

#### 2. Proteostasis Pivot: Activation of the Ubiquitin–Proteasome System (UPS)

-   **Statistically robust UPS enrichment:** Beyond transcriptional regulators, the only other functional axis surviving strict FDR filtering in GO BP is the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway, marked by *Ubiquitin-Dependent Protein Catabolic Process* (\~44 genes), *Protein Ubiquitination* (\~44 genes), and *Proteasomal Protein Catabolic Process* (\~27 genes; all $p_{\text{adj}} \le 0.0035$).

-   **Exclusion of unconfirmed cytoplasmic hits:** Candidate pathways that appeared under unadjusted p-values—most notably *Autophagy*, *MAPK signaling*, and *AMPK signaling* in KEGG, as well as *Autophagosome*, *Vacuolar Membrane*, and chromatin-modifying complexes in GO CC—do not pass `p.adjust < 0.05` against the array background and are therefore excluded from interpretation.

Paired together, the FDR-validated UP and DOWN signatures reveal a sharp compartmental and functional polarity exclusive to H7N9 at 24h: while the virus severely suppresses **cytoplasmic ER–Golgi–lysosomal degradation, secretion, and endolysosomal MHC-II presentation**, the host response pivots sharply toward **nuclear RNA Polymerase II transcriptional remodeling and ubiquitin–proteasome-mediated protein turnover**.

```{r}
kegg_lys <- strsplit(
  enrich_down[["KEGG_2021_Human"]]$Genes[enrich_down[["KEGG_2021_Human"]]$Term == "Lysosome"],

)[[1]]

modules <- list(
  "Core Lysosome"     = unique_down_H7N9[toupper(unique_down_H7N9) %in% kegg_lys],
  "ER-Golgi (N-Glyc)" = strsplit(res_down$geneID[res_down$Description == "Asparagine N-linked glycosylation"], "/")[[1]],
  "MHC-II Axis"       = strsplit(res_down$geneID[res_down$Description == "MHC class II antigen presentation"], "/")[[1]]
)

module_map <- bind_rows(lapply(names(modules), function(m) {
  data.frame(module = m, gene = intersect(unique(modules[[m]]), rownames(data_log)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

expr_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(data_log[unique(module_map$gene), , drop = FALSE])),
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(expr_long) <- c("gene", "SampleID", "expr")

group_means <- expr_long %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "SampleID") %>%
  group_by(gene, Virus, Timepoint) %>%
  summarise(mean_expr = mean(expr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

mock_means <- group_means %>%
  filter(Virus == "mock") %>%
  select(gene, Timepoint, mock_expr = mean_expr)

kin_all <- group_means %>%
  filter(Virus != "mock") %>%
  inner_join(mock_means, by = c("gene", "Timepoint")) %>%
  mutate(
    log2FC = mean_expr - mock_expr,
    time   = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", Timepoint))
  ) %>%
  inner_join(module_map, by = "gene", relationship = "many-to-many")

virus_cols <- c("H3N2" = "#377EB8", "H7N7" = "#FF7F00",
                "H7N9" = "#984EA3", "VN1203" = "#4DAF4A")

# Tier 1: Module-level kinetics (mean +/- SE)
kin_mod <- kin_all %>%
  group_by(module, Virus, time) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_fc = mean(log2FC, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_fc   = sd(log2FC, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(kin_mod, aes(time, mean_fc, color = Virus, fill = Virus, group = Virus)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = virus_cols) +

  facet_wrap(~ module, nrow = 1) +

  labs(title = "Endomembrane & MHC-II Module Kinetics (H7N9-Exclusive Downregulated Genes)",
       x = "Hours post-infection", y = "Mean log2FC vs time-matched mock (+/- SE)")

# Tier 2: Top 4 sentinel genes per module ranked by 24h H7N9 downregulation

  filter(Virus == "H7N9", time == max(time)) %>%
```

## Statistics on Lysosome, Golgi and MHC-II kinetics

Because candidate modules and sentinel genes were defined from the 24h H7N9-exclusive DEG signature, 24h ANOVA significance is reported descriptively to quantify direct inter-strain separation (Dunnett contrasts vs. H7N9), whereas the 3h–12h tests provide an unbiased evaluation of divergence onset.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

kegg_lys <- strsplit(
  enrich_down[["KEGG_2021_Human"]]$Genes[enrich_down[["KEGG_2021_Human"]]$Term == "Lysosome"],
  ";"
)[[1]]

modules <- list(
  "Core Lysosome"     = unique_down_H7N9[toupper(unique_down_H7N9) %in% kegg_lys],
  "ER-Golgi (N-Glyc)" = strsplit(res_down$geneID[res_down$Description == "Asparagine N-linked glycosylation"], "/")[[1]],
  "MHC-II Axis"       = strsplit(res_down$geneID[res_down$Description == "MHC class II antigen presentation"], "/")[[1]]
)

module_map <- bind_rows(lapply(names(modules), function(m) {
  data.frame(module = m, gene = intersect(unique(modules[[m]]), rownames(data_log)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

expr_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(data_log[unique(module_map$gene), , drop = FALSE])),
                           stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(expr_long) <- c("gene", "SampleID", "expr")

mock_means <- expr_long %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "SampleID") %>%
  filter(Virus == "mock") %>%
  group_by(gene, Timepoint) %>%
  summarise(mock_expr = mean(expr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

kin_rep <- expr_long %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "SampleID") %>%
  filter(Virus != "mock") %>%
  inner_join(mock_means, by = c("gene", "Timepoint")) %>%
  mutate(
    lfc   = expr - mock_expr,
    time  = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", Timepoint)),
    Virus = factor(Virus, levels = c("H7N9", "H3N2", "H7N7", "VN1203"))
  ) %>%
  inner_join(module_map, by = "gene", relationship = "many-to-many")

kin_all <- kin_rep %>%
  group_by(gene, Virus, Timepoint, time, module) %>%
  summarise(log2FC = mean(lfc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

virus_cols <- c("H7N9" = "#984EA3", "H3N2" = "#377EB8",
                "H7N7" = "#FF7F00", "VN1203" = "#4DAF4A")

run_time_stats <- function(df, id_col) {
  ids   <- unique(df[[id_col]])
  times <- sort(unique(df$time))
  
  anova_res <- bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(id) {
    bind_rows(lapply(times, function(t) {
      dt  <- df[df[[id_col]] == id & df$time == t, ]
      fit <- aov(lfc ~ Virus, data = dt)
      s   <- summary(fit)[[1]]
      rownames(s) <- trimws(rownames(s))
      data.frame(feature = id, time = t,
                 F_value = round(s["Virus", "F value"], 1),
                 p_value = s["Virus", "Pr(>F)"],
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }))
  
  anova_res$p_adj  <- p.adjust(anova_res$p_value, method = "BH")
  anova_res$signif <- as.character(cut(anova_res$p_adj,
                                       breaks = c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf),
                                       labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns")))
  names(anova_res)[1] <- id_col
  
  posthoc_res <- bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(id) {
    bind_rows(lapply(times, function(t) {
      dt  <- df[df[[id_col]] == id & df$time == t, ]
      fit <- aov(lfc ~ Virus, data = dt)
      ct  <- as.data.frame(contrast(emmeans(fit, ~ Virus), method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1))
      data.frame(feature = id, time = t, contrast = ct$contrast,
                 diff_vs_H7N9 = round(ct$estimate, 2),
                 p_adj = signif(ct$p.value, 3),
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }))
  names(posthoc_res)[1] <- id_col
  
  list(anova = anova_res, posthoc = posthoc_res)
}

# Intersection-union Dunnett summary: significant only when H7N9 < all 3 other strains
make_h7n9_stars <- function(stats_obj, id_col) {
  stats_obj$posthoc %>%
    group_by(.data[[id_col]], time) %>%
    summarise(
      all_lower = all(diff_vs_H7N9 > 0),
      max_p     = max(p_adj),
      .groups   = "drop"
    ) %>%
    left_join(select(stats_obj$anova, all_of(id_col), time, anova_padj = p_adj),
              by = c(id_col, "time")) %>%
    mutate(
      eff_p  = ifelse(all_lower & anova_padj < 0.05, max_p, 1),
      signif = as.character(cut(eff_p,
                                breaks = c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf),
                                labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns")))
    )
}


# Tier 1: Module-level kinetics (1 score per biological replicate)
mod_rep <- kin_rep %>%
  group_by(module, SampleID, Virus, time) %>%
  summarise(lfc = mean(lfc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

mod_stats <- run_time_stats(mod_rep, "module")
mod_h7n9  <- make_h7n9_stars(mod_stats, "module")

mod_sum <- mod_rep %>%
  group_by(module, Virus, time) %>%
  summarise(mean_fc = mean(lfc), se_fc = sd(lfc) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

mod_stars <- mod_sum %>%
  group_by(module) %>%
  summarise(y_pos = max(mean_fc + se_fc) + 0.08 * mod_span, .groups = "drop") %>%

        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")) +

       subtitle = "Mean +/- SEM; stars show Dunnett max(p_adj) where H7N9 < all 3 other strains (*** p < 0.001, ** p < 0.01, * p < 0.05, ns)",

  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  geom_text(data = gene_stars, aes(time, y_pos, label = signif), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_color_manual(values = virus_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(gene_sum$time))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.16))) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene_label, ncol = 4) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold")) +
  labs(title = "Sentinel Gene Kinetics Across the ER-Golgi-Lysosome-MHC-II Axis",
       subtitle = "Mean +/- SEM; stars show Dunnett max(p_adj) where H7N9 < all 3 other strains (*** p < 0.001, ** p < 0.01, * p < 0.05, ns)",
       x = "Hours post-infection", y = "log2 Fold Change vs time-matched mock")
print(p_genes)

# Summary & Post-Hoc Tables
format_wide_signif <- function(df, id_col) {
  tmp <- as.data.frame(df[order(df$time), c(id_col, "time", "signif")])
  tmp$time <- paste0(tmp$time, "h")
  w <- reshape(tmp, idvar = id_col, timevar = "time", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("^signif\\.", "", names(w))
  w
}

knitr::kable(format_wide_signif(mod_stats$anova, "module"), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Module-Level Global One-Way ANOVA Across Viruses (BH-Adjusted)")

knitr::kable(format_wide_signif(mod_h7n9, "module"), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Module-Level H7N9 Exclusivity Summary (ANOVA-Gated Worst-Case Dunnett p_adj)")

knitr::kable(filter(mod_stats$posthoc, time %in% c(12, 24)), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Module-Level Dunnett Post-Hoc Contrasts vs H7N9 at 12h and 24h (Other - H7N9)")

knitr::kable(format_wide_signif(gene_stats$anova, "gene"), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Sentinel Gene Global One-Way ANOVA Across Viruses (BH-Adjusted across 48 tests)")

knitr::kable(format_wide_signif(gene_h7n9, "gene"), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Sentinel Gene H7N9 Exclusivity Summary (ANOVA-Gated Worst-Case Dunnett p_adj)")

module_summary <- kin_all %>%
  filter(Virus == "H7N9", time == max(time)) %>%
  arrange(module, log2FC) %>%
  group_by(module) %>%
  summarise(N_genes = n(), Genes = paste(gene, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(module_summary, col.names = c("Module", "Count", "H7N9-Exclusive Downregulated Genes (sorted by 24h log2FC)"))

shared_genes <- module_map %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  summarise(Modules = paste(module, collapse = " + "), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(shared_genes, caption = "Genes Bridging Multiple Endomembrane/MHC-II Modules")

write.csv(mod_stats$anova,    file.path(output_dir, "module_anova_global.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(gene_stats$anova,   file.path(output_dir, "sentinel_anova_global.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9

# Order unique genes by module and 24h H7N9 downregulation
hm_genes <- kin_all %>%
  filter(Virus == "H7N9", time == max(time)) %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(
    Module = if (n() > 1) "Shared" else first(module),
    fc_24h = first(log2FC),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Module = factor(Module, levels = c("Core Lysosome", "ER-Golgi (N-Glyc)", "MHC-II Axis", "Shared"))) %>%
  arrange(Module, fc_24h)
  # Optional: add `%>% filter(gene %in% top_sentinels$gene)` to plot only the 12 sentinels

# Build chronologically ordered log2FC matrix (genes x Virus_Timepoint)
virus_order <- c("H3N2", "H7N7", "VN1203", "H7N9")
time_order  <- sort(unique(kin_all$time))
col_grid    <- expand.grid(time = time_order, Virus = virus_order, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
col_grid$col_id <- paste0(col_grid$Virus, "_", col_grid$time, "h")

kin_uniq <- kin_all %>%
  distinct(gene, Virus, time, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(col_id = paste0(Virus, "_", time, "h"))

mat_fc <- tapply(kin_uniq$log2FC, list(kin_uniq$gene, kin_uniq$col_id), mean)
mat_fc <- mat_fc[hm_genes$gene, col_grid$col_id, drop = FALSE]

# Clamp values to [-3, 3] so extreme fold changes saturate cleanly without turning grey
max_lim <- 3
mat_plot <- pmax(pmin(mat_fc, max_lim), -max_lim)

# Annotations and visual separators
ann_col <- data.frame(
  Virus = factor(col_grid$Virus, levels = virus_order),
  Time  = factor(paste0(col_grid$time, "h"), levels = paste0(time_order, "h")),
  row.names = col_grid$col_id
)

mod_levels <- levels(droplevels(hm_genes$Module))
ann_row <- data.frame(
  Module = factor(hm_genes$Module, levels = mod_levels),
  row.names = hm_genes$gene
)

mod_palette <- c(
  "Core Lysosome"     = "#D95F02",
  "ER-Golgi (N-Glyc)" = "#1B9E77",
  "MHC-II Axis"       = "#7570B3",
  "Shared"            = "#E7298A"
)

ann_colors <- list(
  Virus  = c(H3N2 = "#377EB8", H7N7 = "#FF7F00", VN1203 = "#4DAF4A", H7N9 = "#984EA3"),
  Time   = setNames(c("#F0F0F0", "#BDBDBD", "#737373", "#252525"), paste0(time_order, "h")),
  Module = mod_palette[mod_levels]
)

col_gaps <- seq(length(time_order), nrow(col_grid) - 1, by = length(time_order))
row_gaps <- cumsum(table(ann_row$Module))
row_gaps <- row_gaps[-length(row_gaps)]

pheatmap(
  mat_plot,
  cluster_rows      = FALSE,
  cluster_cols      = FALSE,
  annotation_col    = ann_col,
  annotation_row    = ann_row,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  gaps_col          = col_gaps,
  gaps_row          = row_gaps,
  labels_col        = paste0(col_grid$time, "h"),
  color             = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(100),
  breaks            = seq(-max_lim, max_lim, length.out = 101),
  fontsize_row      = 7,
  fontsize_col      = 8,
  border_color      = NA,
  main              = "Temporal Expression of H7N9-Exclusive Endomembrane & MHC-II Modules (log2FC vs Mock)"
)
```

## GSEA

```{r}
library(enrichplot)

make_ranked_entrez <- function(deg_df) {
  mapped <- bitr(deg_df$Gene, fromType = "SYMBOL", toType = "ENTREZID", OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db)
  df <- deg_df %>%
    inner_join(mapped, by = c("Gene" = "SYMBOL"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    filter(!is.na(logFC)) %>%
    group_by(ENTREZID) %>%
    slice_max(abs(logFC), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(desc(logFC))
  setNames(df$logFC, df$ENTREZID)
}

deg_list <- list(H3N2 = deg_H3N2, H7N7 = deg_H7N7, VN1203 = deg_VN1203, H7N9 = deg_H7N9)
ranks    <- lapply(deg_list, make_ranked_entrez)

set.seed(42)
gsea_kegg <- lapply(ranks, function(r) {
  gseKEGG(geneList = r, organism = "hsa", pvalueCutoff = 1, verbose = FALSE)
})

# Compare KEGG Lysosome (hsa04142) across all 4 viruses without filtering out non-significant strains
lys_comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(names(gsea_kegg), function(v) {
  as.data.frame(gsea_kegg[[v]]) %>%
    filter(ID == "hsa04142") %>%
    transmute(Virus = v, NES, pvalue, p.adjust, setSize)
}))
knitr::kable(lys_comparison, digits = 4, caption = "KEGG Lysosome (hsa04142) GSEA Across Influenza Strains at 24h")

# Classic running-score plot for H7N9 Lysosome
gseaplot2(gsea_kegg[["H7N9"]], geneSetID = "hsa04142",
          title = "GSEA: KEGG Lysosome in H7N9 (24h vs Mock)")
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)
gsea_kegg <- lapply(ranks, function(r) {
  gseKEGG(geneList = r, organism = "hsa", pvalueCutoff = 1, eps = 0, verbose = FALSE)
})

gsea_react <- lapply(ranks, function(r) {
  gsePathway(geneList = r, organism = "human", pvalueCutoff = 1, eps = 0, verbose = FALSE)
})

# Clean 4-virus comparison across all three endomembrane/MHC-II axes
extract_gsea <- function(gsea_list, term_pattern, col_name = "Description") {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(gsea_list), function(v) {
    df <- as.data.frame(gsea_list[[v]])
    df[grepl(term_pattern, df[[col_name]], ignore.case = TRUE), ] %>%
      transmute(
        Pathway  = Description,
        Virus    = v,
        NES      = round(NES, 3),
        pvalue   = formatC(pvalue, format = "e", digits = 2),
        p.adjust = formatC(p.adjust, format = "e", digits = 2),
        setSize
      )
  }))
}

gsea_summary <- bind_rows(
  extract_gsea(gsea_kegg,  "^hsa04142$", col_name = "ID"),
  extract_gsea(gsea_react, "^Asparagine N-linked glycosylation$|^MHC class II antigen presentation$")
)

gsea_summary <- gsea_summary %>%
  mutate(Virus = factor(Virus, levels = c("H3N2", "H7N7", "VN1203", "H7N9"))) %>%
  arrange(Pathway, Virus)

knitr::kable(gsea_summary, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Cross-Virus GSEA Comparison Across the Endomembrane and MHC-II Axes (24h vs Mock)")

# Multi-pathway running score plot in H7N9 (Reactome)
react_ids <- as.data.frame(gsea_react[["H7N9"]]) %>%
  filter(Description %in% c("Asparagine N-linked glycosylation", "MHC class II antigen presentation")) %>%
  pull(ID)

gseaplot2(gsea_react[["H7N9"]], geneSetID = react_ids,
          title = "GSEA: ER-Golgi Glycosylation & MHC-II in H7N9 (24h vs Mock)")
```
